def max_calm_group_sum(n, a, b):
    max_sum = 0
    
    # Check all pairs of students
    for i, j in combinations(range(n), 2):
        ai, aj = a[i], a[j]
        bi, bj = b[i], b[j]
        
        # Check if student i thinks student j is better
        i_better_than_j = (ai & ~aj) != 0
        
        # Check if student j thinks student i is better
        j_better_than_i = (aj & ~ai) != 0
        
        # If neither student thinks the other is better, they can work together calmly
        if not i_better_than_j and not j_better_than_i:
            max_sum = max(max_sum, bi + bj)
    
    return max_sum

def max_calm_group_sum(n: int, a: List[int], b: List[int]) -> int:
    # Initialize dp array with -1
    dp = [-1] * (1 << n)
    dp[0] = 0
    
    # Iterate over each student
    for i in range(n):
        # Update dp array in reverse to avoid overwriting values used in the current iteration
        for mask in range((1 << n) - 1, (1 << i) - 1, -1):
            if dp[mask ^ (1 << i)] != -1:
                # Check calmness condition
                if all(a[i] & (1 << j) == a[j] & (1 << j) for j in range(i)):
                    dp[mask] = max(dp[mask], dp[mask ^ (1 << i)] + b[i])
    
    # Find the maximum sum for groups with at least two students
    return max(max(dp), 0)
